findings.problem: The hint doesn't rule out encargarse, which is just as common as ocuparse in Latin America for handling a task (yo me encargo de todo), so a learner could give a right answer and still be marked wrong.
findings.fix: hint: handle a task or problem; the reflexive form of 'to occupy', not encargarse

back.es: ocuparse (de): to take care of, deal with, handle (a task or matter); literally to occupy oneself
back.example: Relax / Don't worry, I'll take care of everything.

note: You could show ocuparse with its preposition (ocuparse de) in the answer or grammar, since the verb almost always takes de in this meaning.
